builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: When Relevant Code Is Wrong: Runtime-Aware Context for AI Coding Agents
summary: The method replaces purely relevance-, similarity-, or recency-based retrieval of code and development artifacts with retrieval filtered by operational validity under deployment-specific feature flags, configurations, and architectural evolution. It costs additional infrastructure to link repository artifacts to runtime configurations and maintain classification rules, plus ongoing curation as deployments change, and the evaluation is limited to six tasks and three deployments with reference rules rather than demonstrated gains in agent correctness. It can fail when runtime configuration data is incomplete or stale, when the valid/invalid/unknown classification rules do not match an organization's deployment logic, or when valid recall drops sharply if feature-flag evidence is missing.
rationale: The idea is directly relevant to production coding-agent retrieval, but the paper demonstrates feasibility on a tiny prototype with no measured improvement in agent output quality, so a small-scale pilot against the reader's own repositories is warranted before adoption.
technique: Runtime-aware operational context validity retrieval for coding agents

claims.statement: The method replaces purely relevance-, similarity-, or recency-based retrieval of code and development artifacts with retrieval filtered by operational validity under deployment-specific feature flags, configurations, and architectural evolution. It costs additional infrastructure to link repository artifacts to runtime configurations and maintain classification rules, plus ongoing curation as deployments change, and the evaluation is limited to six tasks and three deployments with reference rules rather than demonstrated gains in agent correctness. It can fail when runtime configuration data is incomplete or stale, when the valid/invalid/unknown classification rules do not match an organization's deployment logic, or when valid recall drops sharply if feature-flag evidence is missing.

Conventional retrieval exposed 16 incompatible artifact occurrences as actionable, while CASE excluded all 16 and retained all applicable artifacts; recency filtering reduced valid recall to 0.43, and removing feature-flag evidence reduced CASE recall to 0.13.
